- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true values show strong upward momentum.
- Overreacts to recent price spikes, producing exaggerated peaks that don’t materialize in true outcomes.
- Tends to underestimate the magnitude of late-stage price increases, especially when historical mean reversion is weak.
- Shows persistent bias toward higher values in the first 10–15 forecast days, suggesting lag in adjusting to recent downward trends.
- When true values rise sharply after a dip, model fails to capture the full extent of the rebound, underestimating the peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after spikes, then undercorrects in subsequent periods, leading to oscillatory errors.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the final 5–7 days, especially when true values are trending upward or consolidating.
